To reproduce all panels in this figure you need to download the data (Figure1_metaDat.csv) from the EGA repository (see Readme.txt).

## Panel a

```{r, echo=T,eval=T}

# ============================================================
# Fig1/code/panel_a_donuts.R
# Panel a: donut charts of molecular group repartition per arm
# ============================================================
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

source("Figure1/00_colors.R")
source("Figure1/01_load_data.R")

plot_panel_a <- function(meta) {
  
  panel_a_dat <- meta %>%
    select(arm, MG) %>%
    filter(!is.na(arm), !is.na(MG)) %>%
    count(arm, MG, name = "n") %>%
    group_by(arm) %>%
    mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  ggplot(panel_a_dat, aes(x = 2, y = n, fill = MG)) +
    geom_col(color = "white", width = 1) +
    geom_text(aes(label = n), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3.2) +
    coord_polar(theta = "y") +
    xlim(0.5, 2.5) +                     # creates the donut hole
    scale_fill_manual(values = mg_colors, name = "MG", drop = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(~ arm, nrow = 1) +
    theme_void(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
      legend.position = "right"
    )
}

# --- usage ---
 meta <- load_figure1_data("Figure1/Figure1_metaDat.csv") ###Replace with your path
 p_a  <- plot_panel_a(meta)
 p_a
# ggsave("Fig1/output/panel_a.pdf", p_a, width = 7, height = 3)


```

## Panel b

```{r,echo=T,eval=T,fig.width = 32,fig.height = 8}
# ============================================================
# Fig1/code/panel_b_prisma_heatmap.R
# Panel B: PRISMA gene-expression heatmap with clinical annotations
# ============================================================
library(pheatmap)

source("Figure1/00_colors.R")
source("Figure1/01_load_data.R")   # for load_figure1_data()

plot_panel_b <- function(meta) {
  
  prisma_genes <- c("CD274", "IGHA1", "IGHD", "CD38", "CXCL13")
  pcr_cols     <- paste0("PCR_", prisma_genes, "_norm")
  stopifnot(all(pcr_cols %in% colnames(meta)))
  
  expr_mat <- as.matrix(meta[, pcr_cols])
  rownames(expr_mat) <- meta$ID
  colnames(expr_mat) <- prisma_genes
  
  annotation <- data.frame(
    Response    = meta$Best_response_L1_RECIST,
    IMDC        = meta$IMDC,
    Sarcomatoid = meta$Sarcomatoid,   # display labels (Present/Absent) — was Sarcomatoid_binary
    Rhabdoid    = meta$Rhabdoid,      # display labels (Present/Absent) — was Rhabdoid_binary
    MG          = meta$MG,
    arm         = meta$arm,
    row.names   = meta$ID
  )
  
  breaksList <- seq(-2.5, 2.5, by = 0.1)
  
  pheatmap::pheatmap(
    t(expr_mat),
    cluster_cols       = TRUE,
    cluster_rows       = TRUE,
    show_colnames      = FALSE,
    show_rownames      = TRUE,
    annotation_names_row = TRUE,
    annotation_legend   = TRUE,
    na_col              = "bisque4",
    annotation_colors   = annoCol_panel_b,   # was annoCol
    annotation          = annotation,
    main                = "All patients",
    cellheight          = 10,
    cellwidth           = 10,
    color  = colorRampPalette(hcl.colors(palette = "Spectral", 12, rev = TRUE))(length(breaksList)),
    breaks = breaksList,
    silent = TRUE
  )
}
# --- usage ---
meta <- load_figure1_data("Figure1/Figure1_metaDat.csv") ###Replace with your path
 hm_b <- plot_panel_b(meta)
 hm_b
# ggsave("Fig1/output/panel_b.pdf", hm_b, width = 9, height = 4)
```

## Panel c

```{r,echo=T,eval=T,fig.width=16,fig.height=12}
# ============================================================
# Fig1/code/panel_c_prisma_violins.R
# Panel C: PRISMA score violin/box plots across 5 groupings,
# with pairwise Wilcoxon comparisons (as in the original figure)
# ============================================================
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)
library(patchwork)

source("Figure1/00_colors.R")
source("Figure1/01_load_data.R")
source("Figure1/utils_plot_group_boxplot.R")
make_melted <- function(meta, group_col, value_col = "PRISMA_num") {
  data.frame(
    variable = value_col,
    groups   = meta[[group_col]],
    value    = meta[[value_col]]
  ) %>% na.omit()
}

panel_c_config <- list(
  list(group_col = "MG",              palette = mg_colors,                header = "ccRCC molecular\ngroup"),
  list(group_col = "IMDC",            palette = imdc_colors,               header = "IMDC"),
  list(group_col = "Sarcomatoid", palette = sarcomatoid_binary_colors, header = "Sarcomatoid\nComponent"),
  list(group_col = "Rhabdoid",    palette = rhabdoid_binary_colors,    header = "Rhabdoid\nComponent"),
  list(group_col = "Both_components",    palette = both_components_colors,    header = "Both\nComponents")  # palette still placeholder
)

plot_panel_c <- function(meta) {
  
  subplots <- lapply(seq_along(panel_c_config), function(i) {
    cfg <- panel_c_config[[i]]
    
    res <- plot_group_boxplot(
      data.m        = make_melted(meta, cfg$group_col),
      variable      = "PRISMA_num",
      violin        = TRUE,
      hide_test     = FALSE,
      compare_groups = TRUE,
      alpha         = 0.5,
      plot_outlier  = TRUE,
      specify_col   = cfg$palette,
      size_point    = 0,
      title_size    = 8,
      add_jitter    = TRUE,
      labs          = c("", "", "PRISMA score")
    )
    
    p <- res[[1]] +
      ggtitle(cfg$header) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 10))
    
    if (i > 1) p <- p + ylab(NULL)   # only the first sub-panel keeps the y-axis label
    p
  })
  
  wrap_plots(subplots, nrow = 1)
}

# --- usage ---
meta <- load_figure1_data("Figure1/Figure1_metaDat.csv") ###Replace with your path
 p_c  <- plot_panel_c(meta)
 p_c
# ggsave("Fig1/output/panel_c.pdf", p_c, width = 16, height = 3.5)

```

## Panel d

```{r,echo=T,eval=T}
# ============================================================
# Fig1/code/panel_d_prisma_response_violins.R
# Panel D: PRISMA score (continuous) by aggregated response (R/NR),
# one violin pair per treatment arm.
# ============================================================
library(dplyr)
library(gridExtra)

source("Figure1/00_colors.R")
source("Figure1/01_load_data.R")
source("Figure1/utils_plot_group_boxplot.R")

add_agg_response <- function(meta) {
  # NOTE: preserved verbatim from your original logic — "NE" (non-evaluable)
  # falls into "NR" here since ifelse() has no third branch. Flagging this:
  # worth deciding if NE should be NA/excluded instead before this goes final.
  meta %>%
    mutate(
      Agg_response = ifelse(Best_response_L1_RECIST %in% c("PR", "CR"), "R", "NR"),
      Agg_response = factor(Agg_response, levels = c("R", "NR"))
    )
}

plot_panel_d <- function(meta) {
  
  meta <- add_agg_response(meta)
  
  plots <- lapply(comp_list, function(comp) {
    melted <- meta %>%
      filter(arm == comp) %>%
      melt_df(var_to_group = "Agg_response") %>%
      na.omit()
    
    res <- plot_group_boxplot(
      data.m        = melted,
      variable      = "PRISMA_num",
      violin        = TRUE,
      hide_test     = FALSE,
      compare_groups = TRUE,
      alpha         = 0.5,
      ylim          = c(-3, 3),
      plot_outlier  = TRUE,
      specify_col   = rev(rep_2_colors),
      size_point    = 0,
      title_size    = 8,
      add_jitter    = TRUE,
      labs          = c("", "", comp)
    )
    
    res[[1]] + theme(plot.title = element_blank())
  })
  
  grid.arrange(grobs = plots, ncol = 1)
}

# --- usage ---
meta <- load_figure1_data("Figure1/Figure1_metaDat.csv") ###Replace with your path
# pdf("Fig1/output/panel_d.pdf", width = 8, height = 12)
 plot_panel_d(meta)
# dev.off()
```

## Panel e

```{r,echo=T,eval=T,fig.width=10,fig.height=18}
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)

source("Figure1/00_colors.R")
source("Figure1/01_load_data.R")
source("Figure1/utils_plot_group_boxplot.R") 

plot_panel_e <- function(meta, test_name = "fisher.test") {
  
  meta <- add_agg_response(meta)
  
  meta <- meta %>%
    filter(Best_response_L1_RECIST != "NE") %>%          # <- drop NE
    mutate(Best_response_L1_RECIST = factor(Best_response_L1_RECIST,
                                            levels = c("CR", "PR", "SD", "PD")))
  
  arms <- c("Nivo-Ipi", "Nivo", "TKI")
  
  plots_agg <- lapply(arms, function(arm_f) {
    clin_f <- meta %>% filter(arm == arm_f) %>% as.data.frame()   # <- fix: drop tibble class
    plot_contingency(clin_f, c("PRISMA", "Agg_response"),
                     inverse_factor2 = TRUE, labs = c("", "%", "Response"),
                     create_labels = FALSE, palette = rev(rep_2_colors),
                     test_name = test_name, title = arm_f)[[1]]
  })
  
  plots_full <- lapply(arms, function(arm_f) {
    clin_f <- meta %>% filter(arm == arm_f) %>% as.data.frame()   # <- fix: drop tibble class
    plot_contingency(clin_f, c("PRISMA", "Best_response_L1_RECIST"),
                     inverse_factor2 = TRUE, labs = c("", "%", "Response"),
                     create_labels = FALSE, palette = response_colors,
                     test_name = test_name, title = arm_f)[[1]]
  })
  
  wrap_plots(
    c(plots_agg[1], plots_full[1], plots_agg[2], plots_full[2], plots_agg[3], plots_full[3]),
    ncol = 2, nrow = 3
  )
}

# --- usage ---
meta <- load_figure1_data("Figure1/Figure1_metaDat.csv") ###Replace with your path
# pdf("Fig1/output/panel_e.pdf", width = 10, height = 14)
 plot_panel_e(meta)
# dev.off()

```

## Panel f-h

```{r,echo=T,eval=T}
library(dplyr)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(patchwork)

source("Figure1/00_colors.R")
source("Figure1/01_load_data.R")

# --- fallbacks for undefined theme helpers — REPLACE with your real ones ---
theme_for_ggsurv <- ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 8)   # 
clean_theme_fn   <- function() survminer::theme_cleantable() # 

surv_vars <- list(
  PFS = c("PFS", "PFS_status"),
  OS  = c("OS",  "OS_status"),
  TST = c("TST", "TST_status")
)
comp_list <- c("Nivo-Ipi", "Nivo", "TKI")

#
prisma_level_order <- c("PRISMA-high", "PRISMA-low")


one_km_plot <- function(data, arm_label, endpoint_label, time_col, event_col,
                        group_col = "PRISMA", palette_named) {
  
  d <- data %>%
    filter(arm == arm_label) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%                       # guard against tibble subsetting bugs
    select(time = all_of(time_col), alive = all_of(event_col), group = all_of(group_col)) %>%
    mutate(time = as.numeric(as.character(time)),
           group = factor(group, levels = prisma_level_order)) %>%
    na.omit()
  
  pal <- unname(palette_named[levels(droplevels(d$group))])  # order-safe lookup by level name
  
  fit <- survfit(Surv(time, alive) ~ group, data = d)
  
  pl <- ggsurvplot(
    fit, data = d, pval = FALSE, break.time.by = 10, fun = "pct",
    palette = pal, conf.int = FALSE, surv.median.line = "hv",
    legend.labs = levels(droplevels(d$group)),
    risk.table = FALSE, ggtheme = theme_for_ggsurv,
    fontsize = 2, tables.theme = clean_theme_fn(), risk.table.title = ""
  )
  
  p_value <- surv_pvalue(fit = fit, data = d)$pval
  
  pl$plot <- pl$plot +
    ylab(paste0("% ", arm_label)) + xlab("Months") +
    ggtitle(paste0("n= ", nrow(d), "\n", endpoint_label)) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
  
  medians <- sort(surv_median(fit)$median)
  label_y_positions <- 4
  pl$plot <- pl$plot +
    annotate("label", x = medians + c(-2, 2), y = label_y_positions,
             label = round(medians, 2), colour = pal, size = 2) +
    annotate("text", x = 30, y = 100, size = 3.5,
             label = paste0("p = ", round(p_value, 4)))
  
  pl$plot
}

plot_panel_fgh <- function(meta) {
  
  all_plots <- lapply(comp_list, function(comp) {
    lapply(names(surv_vars), function(ep) {
      one_km_plot(
        data           = meta,
        arm_label      = comp,
        endpoint_label = ep,
        time_col       = surv_vars[[ep]][1],
        event_col      = surv_vars[[ep]][2],
        palette_named  = c(
          "PRISMA-high" = unname(survival_hilo_colors[[comp]]["High"]),
          "PRISMA-low"  = unname(survival_hilo_colors[[comp]]["Low"])
        )
      )
    })
  }) %>% unlist(recursive = FALSE)
  
  wrap_plots(all_plots, ncol = 3, nrow = 3)
}

# --- usage ---
meta <- load_figure1_data("Figure1/Figure1_metaDat.csv") 
# pdf("Fig1/output/panel_fgh.pdf", width = 12, height = 10)
 plot_panel_fgh(meta)
# dev.off()
```
